prompt: Match each family of question to Faro's version of it.

pairs.right: Whose timestamp says a box was late?
Is it the delay or the region?

right_distractors: Which font is the deck in?

prompt: Which family of question is most dangerous for a finding like Faro's?
hint: If it lands, the finding dissolves.

choices.text: Size, because a small effect is easy to dismiss
choices.why: Size is answered with arithmetic.

choices.text: Cost, because nobody approves spending
choices.why: The recommended option costs nothing new.

choices.text: Cause
choices.why: If region explained it, fixing deliveries would change little.

choices.text: Source
choices.why: Answered with a definition.

prompt: Sandra asks "did you include the interior?". What may the question underneath be?
hint: The family rarely asked in its own words.

choices.text: Are you about to tell Paulo my team is the problem?
choices.why: Blame often hides behind a source or cause question.

choices.text: How big is the interior?
choices.why: A size question, taken literally.

choices.text: What does the pilot cost?
choices.why: Cost, and not what she asked.

choices.text: Is the data from 2025?
choices.why: Source, and already stated.

prompt: Why does checking inside each region test the objection?

choices.text: Because regions have different carriers and so different on-time rates
choices.why: One carrier serves both.

choices.text: Because the board asked to see the regions separately last quarter
choices.why: Not the reason.

choices.text: Because smaller groups are always more accurate
choices.why: Smaller groups are noisier, not more accurate.

choices.text: Region is held fixed
choices.why: If the gap vanished inside each region, region would be the explanation.

prompt: To one decimal place, what is the cancellation rate for late first deliveries in the interior?
How many points is the gap between late and on-time customers in the capital?
The pooled gap is 24.1 points, a little more than either region's. What does that difference show?

choices.text: A calculation error
choices.why: Calc confirms all three.

choices.text: The part of the gap that region explains
choices.why: The interior's higher churn and higher late share inflate the pooled number slightly.

choices.text: That the capital matters more
choices.why: Not what the difference measures.

choices.text: That the finding is false and the delay explains little
choices.why: Most of the gap survives inside each region.

prompt: Comparing inside groups that share a possible cause is called ___.
What does the regional check not rule out?

choices.text: Differences the table does not record
choices.why: New streets, the cheapest delivery option; lesson 12 returns to them.

choices.text: That the interior has more late boxes than the capital does
choices.why: That is a fact the check uses, not something it rules out.

choices.text: That region explains the whole gap
choices.why: That is exactly what it does rule out.

choices.text: Nothing: the cause is proved
choices.why: Removing one explanation does not prove the cause.

prompt: What does a premortem ask people to imagine?

choices.text: That the project or meeting has already failed, and why
choices.why: Treating failure as having happened frees people to say why.

choices.text: The best possible outcome
choices.why: The opposite.

choices.text: What a competitor would do
choices.why: Not this technique.

choices.text: The budget
choices.why: No.

prompt: Why is Diego a good red team for Marina's deck?

choices.text: He is the most senior analyst at Faro and can overrule her conclusions
choices.why: Seniority is not the reason.

choices.text: He wrote the original delivery reports from scratch years ago
choices.why: Not stated, and not the reason.

choices.text: He has never seen the data before, so he reads it fresh
choices.why: He knows the data well; that is the point.

choices.text: His objections are Sandra's
choices.why: He knows the business and will raise what she will raise.

prompt: What belongs in the appendix, by the lesson?

choices.text: The charts that did not make the main deck
choices.why: That makes it too long to search in two seconds.

choices.text: One slide for each likely question
choices.why: Each with an assertion title, nothing else.

choices.text: The speaker notes
choices.why: Not slides.

choices.text: A thank-you slide
choices.why: No.

prompt: How many slides does Faro's appendix have?
Put the four moves of a good answer in order.
You do not know the answer. What does the lesson say to do?

choices.text: Give your best guess confidently, then check afterwards
choices.why: A wrong guess discredits everything said before it.

choices.text: Change the subject to the recommendation
choices.why: Evasion is noticed.

choices.text: Say so, what you need, and when
choices.why: Then deliver by the date you gave.

choices.text: Ask the questioner
choices.why: Not the advice.

prompt: Why repeat a question before answering it?

choices.text: To show the questioner you are taking them more seriously than the others in the room
choices.why: Not the reason.

choices.text: To correct the way it was worded so that it fits the slides you prepared
choices.why: Rewording to suit you is evasion.

choices.text: Because it is polite and expected in any formal meeting
choices.why: Politeness is not the reason given.

choices.text: The room hears it; you get seconds
choices.why: If the room may not have heard it, repeating it helps both.

prompt: A manager restates their own view and ends with "don't you think?". How does the lesson treat it?

choices.text: As a real question that needs the four moves in full
choices.why: It is a statement; answering it in full makes a debate.

choices.text: As a comment: acknowledge, connect, move on
choices.why: Arguing with a statement eats the time for the decision.

choices.text: As an attack
choices.why: Not every statement is hostile.

choices.text: Ignore it
choices.why: Acknowledge it first.

prompt: "So you're saying my team is failing?" What is the worst response, by the lesson?
hint: It hears blame as a challenge to the data.

choices.text: Defending the analysis: the numbers are what they are
choices.why: True, and it answers the wrong question.

choices.text: Using her own on-time rate respectfully
choices.why: That is part of the better response.

choices.text: Giving her team a role in the fix
choices.why: Also part of the better one.

choices.text: Saying she is not being blamed
choices.why: Also part of the better one.

prompt: What principle from Getting to Yes does the lesson borrow?

choices.text: Avoid conceding in public to somebody who is senior to you
choices.why: Not from the book, and not the lesson.

choices.text: Answer every attack with data from the appendix
choices.why: Data does not answer a concern about blame.

choices.text: Separate the people from the problem
choices.why: Talk about the step, the data and the decision, not whose fault it is.

choices.text: Split the difference
choices.why: Not the principle quoted.

prompt: What is the best defence against a hostile question in the meeting, by the lesson?

choices.text: A longer appendix
choices.why: Length does not remove surprise.

choices.text: No surprises: show it to the person first
choices.why: Somebody who helped shape the recommendation will not attack it in public.

choices.text: Present only to Paulo
choices.why: The others still have to act.

choices.text: Ask the most senior person present to stop the questions until the end
choices.why: Postponing an attack does not answer it.
